title: mavai declarative service-definition file (mavai-services/1)
description: Structural schema for the mavai family's declarative service-definition file. It validates the parsed data model of the YAML document. The canonical specification is the prose format specification maintained in the family's internal requirements catalog (MAVAI-SERVICES-FORMAT.md); this schema is its machine-checkable structural projection and never introduces a rule the specification does not state — $comment fields cite the mandating sections. Semantic obligations the schema cannot express (type-registry resolution, factory-signature configuration validation for user types, duplicate-grid-point refusal, provider capability vetoes, ...) are carried by the conformance corpus manifest. These artefacts are family engineering infrastructure — schemas the implementing frameworks conform to — not a standard for third-party implementations.

scalarValue.$comment: SII.7: configuration values are scalars (string, number, boolean) — matching the mavai-explore-1 factors value space.

type.$comment: SII.7: names a service implementation in the type registry — a built-in (language-model) or a user type registered in host code. Registry resolution is semantic, manifest-carried.

configuration.$comment: Part I: exactly one configuration: block — the complete set of covariate values the service runs under; no parameter lives anywhere else in the definition (the uniformity rule).

explorations.$comment: Part I / SII.6: builder-style entries, each declaring only the covariates that deviate from the baseline record. An entry restating the baseline (including an empty entry) is refused — duplicate resolved grid points are semantic, manifest-carried.

configuration.$comment: SII.7: for a user-registered type the factory's signature is the configuration schema (validated by the reader at load time, not expressible here); values are scalars.

system-prompt.$comment: SII.3: required — the system prompt is what turns a model into a service, the defining covariate of a language-model-backed service; a configuration without one is refused.

provider.$comment: SII.3: the named vendor integrations; omitted means the generic OpenAI-compatible protocol against the environment-configured endpoint.

model.$comment: SII.3: optional, with an environment default.

top-p.$comment: SII.3, client-factors amendment 2026-07-17: a number in (0, 1], the nucleus-sampling mass.

thinking.$comment: SII.3, client-factors amendment 2026-07-17: default none. Provider vetoes (anthropic's thinking/sampling exclusion) are semantic, manifest-carried.

prompt-caching.$comment: SII.3, client-factors amendment 2026-07-17: default false; correctness-invariant by construction, stochastic impact confined to latency and cost.

response-schema.$comment: SII.3: an inline mapping — the JSON Schema the model is instructed to satisfy, passed through the provider's structured-output mechanism; a covariate unconditionally (the generation-side rule, 2026-07-17). Per-provider support is a load-time refusal, semantic, manifest-carried.

languageModelConfiguration.$comment: SII.3: the type: language-model configuration block holds every parameter; no parameter may appear outside it. Token-related parameters are deliberately absent from v0. Secrets never appear in this file — credentials are environment-only.

languageModelExplorationEntry.$comment: Part I / SII.6: an exploration entry declares only the covariates that deviate from the baseline record — the same key vocabulary, nothing required.
